children: The holding company of Italian entrepreneur Francesco Gaetano Caltagirone said on Thursday it would vote against Monte dei Paschi di Siena's (MPS) (BPMS.MI) proposals to acquire Banco BPM <BAMI.MI> and Banca Generali
The decision deals a fresh blow to MPS Chief Executive Luigi Lovaglio's efforts to fend off market leader Intesa Sanpaolo's
takeover bid for the Tuscan lender.
Caltagirone's FGC,  which owns 10.26% of MPS, said it would vote against both acquisitions at an Oct. 29 shareholder meeting and that it would also oppose a proposed merger between MPS and Mediobanca
, another pillar of Lovaglio's defence strategy.

Its stance follows decisions by two other major MPS investors - Delfin, the Del Vecchio family's holding company which holds a 17.6% stake, and the Benetton family vehicle Edizione with a 1.45% stake - to back Intesa's improved €35 billion ($39.18 billion) offer for MPS.
Lovaglio unveiled the acquisitions in August as part of a broader strategy aimed at keeping MPS independent and creating a larger financial group capable of resisting Intesa's approach.

Intesa has said it will withdraw its offer if MPS investors endorse Lovaglio's defence plan. As a result, voting against the proposed acquisitions and merger has become the clearest way for shareholders to support Intesa.

While Caltagirone stopped short of formally committing his stake to Intesa's offer, his decision to oppose all three elements of the MPS plan gives Intesa's bid momentum and increases pressure on Lovaglio ahead of the decisive Oct. 29 vote.
